newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ESPN, Star TV form Asia sports JV.
newsitem.headline: ESPN, Star TV form Asia sports JV.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's sports channel ESPN and News Corp Ltd's satellite broadcaster STAR TV said on Friday they are forming an Asian sports programming joint venture combining the resources of STAR Sports and ESPN Asia.
Each of them holds a 50 percent interest in the new company, the two groups said in a joint statement.
Under the terms of the agreement, both the existing ESPN Asia and STAR Sports brands will be preserved.

The new company will provide multiple sports programming services to all territories throughout Asia with the exception of Japan, Australia and New Zealand, where each of the parties has separate, pre-existing ventures.
Alexander Brown, currently managing director of ESPN Asia, will be managing director of the joint venture, and will take direction from representatives of both partners.
The statement did not give further details about the joint venture, such the consideration involved.
Currently, STAR Sports is available primarily to China, Taiwan, India, and other parts of Southeast Asia.
ESPN Asia recently completed construction of a 46,000 square-foot production facility in Singapore from which it distributes networks to Taiwan, Hong Kong, China, Southeast Asia and India.
